The hypothesis tests a spread between two flow rates, each standardized against its own history, and expects a positive IC. That matches claim 5, which describes a spread between two flow rates standardized against their own histories that gave a positive IC (opposite to the predicted sign).

Claim 2 concerns a product of a flow rate and a stock rate, not a spread, so it doesn't apply. Claim 3 covers a cross-sectional rank product of pay growth and hours change, which is also different. Claims 6 and 7 refer to the same finding as claim 5 (stronger in high-T periods, 54% coverage), but the hypothesis does not test those specifics. Claims 1 and 4 are meta-level notes about the report and word limits.

The hypothesis and expression build on claim 5. Claims 6 and 7 are follow-on details of that finding, and the hypothesis does not test them.
